Notes: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the change in the inflation-adjusted value of all goods and services produced by the economy. It is the broadest measure of economic activity and the primary indicator of the economy's health. A higher than expected reading should be taken as positive/bullish for the JPY, while a lower than expected reading should be taken as negative/bearish for the JPY.
Reserve Bank of Australia interest rate decision. Higher than expected readings should be taken as positive/bullish for the AUD.
Job Openings survey measures the number of vacant jobs in the US. Higher than expected values indicate a strong labor market.
Core Consumer Price Index measures monthly change in prices of goods and services excluding food and energy. A higher than expected reading should be taken as positive/bullish for the USD.
Consumer Price Index measures monthly change in prices of goods and services purchased by consumers. A higher than expected reading should be taken as positive/bullish for the USD.
Consumer Price Index (year-over-year) measures annual percentage change in consumer prices. Important inflation indicator affecting monetary policy decisions.
Bank of Canada interest rate decision. Higher than expected readings indicate tightening monetary policy and should be taken as positive/bullish for the CAD.
Federal Reserve interest rate decision is the most important monetary policy announcement. Strongly influences USD and global markets.
Swiss National Bank quarterly interest rate decision. Important for CHF and EUR/CHF currency pairs.
Weekly jobless claims indicate labor market health. Lower than expected values are positive/bullish for the USD.
Monthly GDP growth for the United Kingdom. Higher than expected readings should be taken as positive/bullish for the GBP.
German Consumer Price Index measures monthly change in prices of goods and services. Important inflation indicator for the Eurozone.
